summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, renal and pancreatic transplants, and Charcot foot was admitted for fever and fatigue. She presented with fevers up to 101.7°F and rigors, attributed to a left foot infection in the setting of severe ischemia. Imaging confirmed arterial occlusion at the ankle with poor collateral flow, leading to a left below-knee amputation on hospital day 7. She developed transient shortness of breath due to fluid overload, managed with diuresis and oxygen, with resolution of pulmonary edema. Anemia was noted, likely due to missed erythropoietin injections, and managed with transfusion and Procrit. She remained afebrile after antibiotic treatment, with negative blood cultures. Her transplant medications were adjusted, and she was transitioned to rehab with stable kidney function and improved overall condition.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with gangrene
Cellulitis and abscess of foot, except toes
Diabetes with peripheral circulatory disorders, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
s/p renal and pancreatic transplant with immunosuppression management
